sanskrit: amānuṣāṇi karmāṇi yasyaitāni mahātmanaḥ tena sattvavatā saṃkhye śūreṇāhavaśobhinā kṛtinā samare rājan saṃdhis te tāta yujyatām
english: Superhuman are these deeds of that great-souled one; with him, the resolute, the valiant, who shines in combat and is accomplished in war, O king — let a peace be made with him, my son.

sanskrit: yāvat kṛṣṇo mahābāhuḥ svādhīnaḥ kurusaṃsadi tāvat pārthena śūreṇa saṃdhis te tāta yujyatām
english: While mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa is still amenable in the assembly of the Kurus, even now, my son, let a peace be made with the valiant Pārtha.

sanskrit: yāvac camūṃ na te śeṣāṃ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ nāśayaty arjunas tāvat saṃdhis te tāta yujyatām
english: While Arjuna has not yet destroyed what remains of your army with his straight-jointed arrows, even now, my son, let a peace be made with him.

sanskrit: yāvat tiṣṭhanti samare hataśeṣāḥ sahodarāḥ nṛpāś ca bahavo rājaṃs tāvat saṃdhiḥ prayujyatām
english: While your own brothers, the survivors of the slaughter, and many kings still stand in the battle, O king, even now let a peace be concluded.

sanskrit: na nirdahati te yāvat krodhadīptekṣaṇaś camūm yudhiṣṭhiro hi tāvad vai saṃdhis te tāta yujyatām
english: While Yudhiṣṭhira, his eyes blazing with wrath, has not yet burned up your army, even now, my son, let a peace be made with him.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ yāvac camūṃ mahārāja nāśayanti na sarvaśaḥ tāvat te pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ saubhrātraṃ tāta rocatām
english: While Nakula and Sahadeva, and Bhīmasena the son of Pāṇḍu, have not yet destroyed your army utterly, O great king, even now, my son, let brotherhood with the Pāṇḍavas find favor with you.

sanskrit: yuddhaṃ madantam evāstu tāta saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ etat te rocatāṃ vākyaṃ yad ukto 'si mayānagha etat kṣemam ahaṃ manye tava caiva kulasya ca
english: Let this war end with me, my son; be reconciled with the Pāṇḍavas. May the words I have spoken to you find favor with you, O blameless one. This I judge to be for the welfare of yourself and of your lineage.

sanskrit: tyaktvā manyum upaśāmyasva pārthaiḥ; paryāptam etad yat kṛtaṃ phalgunena bhīṣmasyāntād astu vaḥ sauhṛdaṃ vā; saṃpraśleṣaḥ sādhu rājan prasīda
english: Cast off your wrath and make peace with the Pārthas; enough is the slaughter that Phalguna has wrought. With the passing of Bhīṣma let there be friendship between you; reunion is good, O king — be gracious.

sanskrit: rājyasyārdhaṃ dīyatāṃ pāṇḍavānām; indraprasthaṃ dharmarājo 'nuśāstu mā mitradhruk pārthivānāṃ jaghanyaḥ; pāpāṃ kīrtiṃ prāpsyase kauravendra
english: Let half the kingdom be given to the Pāṇḍavas; let the King of Righteousness rule from Indraprastha. Do not become a betrayer of friends, the basest of kings, lest you win an evil fame, O lord of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: mamāvasānāc chāntir astu prajānāṃ; saṃgacchantāṃ pārthivāḥ prītimantaḥ pitā putraṃ mātulaṃ bhāgineyo; bhrātā caiva bhrātaraṃ praitu rājan
english: With my end let there be peace for the peoples; let the kings come together in gladness. Let father go to son, and nephew to uncle, and brother to brother, O king.

sanskrit: na ced evaṃ prāptakālaṃ vaco me; mohāviṣṭaḥ pratipatsyasy abuddhyā bhīṣmasyāntād etadantāḥ stha sarve; satyām etāṃ bhāratīm īrayāmi
english: But if, sunk in delusion and folly, you do not heed these timely words of mine, then with the end of Bhīṣma all of you shall meet your end — this true word do I declare, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: etad vākyaṃ sauhṛdād āpageyo; madhye rājñāṃ bhārataṃ śrāvayitvā tūṣṇīm āsīc chalyasaṃtaptamarmā; yatvātmānaṃ vedanāṃ saṃnigṛhya
english: Having out of affection made the Bhārata hear these words in the midst of the kings, the son of the river fell silent, his vitals seared by the darts, mastering himself and holding back his pain.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatas te pārthivāḥ sarve jagmuḥ svān ālayān punaḥ tūṣṇīṃbhūte mahārāja bhīṣme śaṃtanunandane
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, when Bhīṣma the delight of Śaṃtanu had fallen silent, O great king, all those kings went back again to their own dwellings.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu nihataṃ bhīṣmaṃ rādheyaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ īṣad āgatasaṃtrāsaḥ tvarayopajagāma ha
english: But when Rādheya, the bull among men, heard that Bhīṣma had been struck down, seized with a touch of fear he came swiftly to him.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ śaratalpagataṃ tadā janmaśayyāgataṃ devaṃ kārttikeyam iva prabhum
english: He beheld the great-souled one lying then upon his bed of arrows, like the god Kārttikeya, the lord, lying upon the couch of his birth.

sanskrit: nimīlitākṣaṃ taṃ vīraṃ sāśrukaṇṭhas tadā vṛṣaḥ abhyetya pādayos tasya nipapāta mahādyutiḥ
english: That hero lay with his eyes closed; and the Bull, his throat choked with tears, of great splendor, drew near and fell down at his feet.

sanskrit: rādheyo 'haṃ kuruśreṣṭha nityaṃ cāṣkigatas tava dveṣyo 'tyantam anāgāḥ sann iti cainam uvāca ha
english: "I am Rādheya, O best of the Kurus, ever before your eyes, hated by you utterly though I had done no wrong" — thus he spoke to him.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā kuruvṛddhaḥ sa balāt saṃvṛttalocanaḥ śanair udvīkṣya sasneham idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing this, the aged Kuru, forcing open his closed eyes, gazed up slowly and with affection spoke these words.

sanskrit: rahitaṃ dhiṣṇyam ālokya samutsārya ca rakṣiṇaḥ piteva putraṃ gāṅgeyaḥ pariṣvajyaikabāhunā
english: Seeing the place was secluded, and having sent away the guards, the son of Gaṅgā embraced him with one arm, as a father embraces a son.

sanskrit: ehy ehi me vipratīpa spardhase tvaṃ mayā saha yadi māṃ nābhigacchethā na te śreyo bhaved dhruvam
english: "Come, come to me, you who set yourself against me, contending with me. Had you not come to me, surely it would not have been well for you.

sanskrit: kaunteyas tvaṃ na rādheyo vidito nāradān mama kṛṣṇadvaipāyanāc caiva keśavāc ca na saṃśayaḥ
english: You are the son of Kuntī, not the son of Rādhā — this I know from Nārada, and from Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, and from Keśava too; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: na ca dveṣo 'sti me tāta tvayi satyaṃ bravīmi te tejovadhanimittaṃ tu paruṣāṇy aham uktavān
english: I bear you no hatred, my son — I speak the truth to you; it was only to curb your fierce energy that I uttered harsh words.

sanskrit: akasmāt pāṇḍavān hi tvaṃ dviṣasīti matir mama yenāsi bahuśo rūkṣaṃ coditaḥ sūryanandana
english: You hate the Pāṇḍavas without cause — such was my thought; and for that reason I goaded you again and again with rough speech, O son of the Sun.

sanskrit: jānāmi samare vīryaṃ śatrubhir duḥsahaṃ tava brahmaṇyatāṃ ca śauryaṃ ca dāne ca paramāṃ gatim
english: I know your prowess in battle, hard for foes to bear, and your reverence for the brahmins, your heroism, and your supreme excellence in giving.

sanskrit: na tvayā sadṛśaḥ kaś cit puruṣeṣv amaropama kulabhedaṃ ca matvāhaṃ sadā paruṣam uktavān
english: There is none among men your equal, O peer of the immortals; yet, fearing a division of the family, I always spoke to you harshly.

sanskrit: iṣvastre bhārasaṃdhāne lāghave 'strabale tathā sadṛśaḥ phalgunenāsi kṛṣṇena ca mahātmanā
english: In archery and missile-craft, in bearing strain, in swiftness, and in the might of your weapons, you are the equal of Phalguna and of the great-souled Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: karṇa rājapuraṃ gatvā tvayaikena dhanuṣmatā tasyārthe kururājasya rājāno mṛditā yudhi
english: O Karṇa, going to the royal city, you alone, bearing your bow, crushed kings in battle for the sake of that king of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tathā ca balavān rājā jarāsaṃdho durāsadaḥ samare samaraślāghī tvayā na sadṛśo 'bhavat
english: And likewise the mighty king Jarāsaṃdha, hard to assail and proud of his warring, proved no match for you in combat.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyaḥ satyavādī ca tejasārka ivāparaḥ devagarbho 'jitaḥ saṃkhye manuṣyair adhiko bhuvi
english: Devoted to the brahmins and truthful in speech, in splendor like a second sun, sprung from a god, unconquered in battle — on earth you surpass all men.

sanskrit: vyapanīto 'dya manyur me yas tvāṃ prati purā kṛtaḥ daivaṃ puruṣakāreṇa na śakyam ativartitum
english: Gone now is the wrath I once nursed against you. Fate cannot be overcome by human effort.

sanskrit: sodaryāḥ pāṇḍavā vīrā bhrātaras te 'risūdana saṃgaccha tair mahābāho mama ced icchasi priyam
english: The heroic Pāṇḍavas are your own brothers, born of the same womb, O slayer of foes. Join with them, mighty-armed one, if you would do what pleases me.

sanskrit: mayā bhavatu nirvṛttaṃ vairam ādityanandana pṛthivyāṃ sarvarājāno bhavantv adya nirāmayāḥ
english: Let this enmity be ended with me, O son of the Sun; let all the kings on earth this day be free of affliction."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca jānāmy ahaṃ mahāprājña sarvam etan na saṃśayaḥ yathā vadasi durdharṣa kaunteyo 'haṃ na sūtajaḥ
english: Karṇa said: I know all this, O greatly wise one; there is no doubt of it. As you say, O unassailable one, I am the son of Kuntī and not born of a charioteer.

sanskrit: avakīrṇas tv ahaṃ kuntyā sūtena ca vivardhitaḥ bhuktvā duryodhanaiśvaryaṃ na mithyā kartum utsahe
english: Yet I was cast off by Kuntī and raised by a charioteer; and having enjoyed Duryodhana's bounty, I cannot now prove false to it.

sanskrit: vasu caiva śarīraṃ ca yad udāraṃ tathā yaśaḥ sarvaṃ duryodhanasyārthe tyaktaṃ me bhūridakṣiṇa kopitāḥ pāṇḍavā nityaṃ mayāśritya suyodhanam
english: My wealth, my body, and my noble fame — all of it I have surrendered for Duryodhana's sake, O giver of abundant gifts; and, taking my stand with Suyodhana, I have ever provoked the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: avaśyabhāvī vai yo 'rtho na sa śakyo nivartitum daivaṃ puruṣakāreṇa ko nivartitum utsahet
english: That which is destined to be cannot be turned aside; who could venture to reverse fate by human effort?

sanskrit: pṛthivīkṣayaśaṃsīni nimittāni pitāmaha bhavadbhir upalabdhāni kathitāni ca saṃsadi
english: The omens foretelling the destruction of the earth, O grandsire, have been perceived by you and declared in the assembly.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavā vāsudevaś ca viditā mama sarvaśaḥ ajeyāḥ puruṣair anyair iti tāṃś cotsahāmahe
english: The Pāṇḍavas and Vāsudeva are known to me in every way as unconquerable by other men; yet even against them we will dare to strive.

sanskrit: anujānīṣva māṃ tāta yuddhe prītamanāḥ sadā anujñātas tvayā vīra yudhyeyam iti me matiḥ
english: Give me your leave, my father, in this war, ever with a glad heart; with your leave, O hero, it is my resolve to fight.

sanskrit: duruktaṃ vipratīpaṃ vā saṃrambhāc cāpalāt tathā yan mayāpakṛtaṃ kiṃ cit tad anukṣantum arhasi
english: Whatever harsh or perverse word I spoke amiss, out of anger or recklessness, whatever offense I have done — you ought to forgive it.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca na cec chakyam athotsraṣṭuṃ vairam etat sudāruṇam anujānāmi karṇa tvāṃ yudhyasva svargakāmyayā
english: Bhīṣma said: If this most dreadful enmity cannot be cast off, then I give you leave, O Karṇa — fight, in your longing for heaven.

sanskrit: vimanyur gatasaṃrambhaḥ kuru karma nṛpasya hi yathāśakti yathotsāhaṃ satāṃ vṛtteṣu vṛttavān
english: Free of wrath, free of agitation, do the king's work, according to your strength and your zeal, abiding by the conduct of the good.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tvām anujānāmi yad icchasi tad āpnuhi kṣatradharmajitāṃl lokān saṃprāpsyasi na saṃśayaḥ
english: I give you my leave; attain what you desire. You shall surely win the worlds conquered by the duty of the warrior — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yudhyasva nirahaṃkāro balavīryavyapāśrayaḥ dharmo hi yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate
english: Fight without pride, relying on your strength and prowess; for there is no higher duty known for a warrior than righteous battle.

sanskrit: praśame hi kṛto yatnaḥ sucirāt suciraṃ mayā na caiva śakitaḥ kartuṃ yato dharmas tato jayaḥ
english: Long and again long have I striven for peace, yet I have not been able to make it; for where there is righteousness, there is victory.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evaṃ bruvantaṃ gāṅgeyam abhivādya prasādya ca rādheyo ratham āruhya prāyāt tava sutaṃ prati
english: Saṃjaya said: When the son of Gaṅgā had thus spoken, Rādheya saluted him and won his grace, then mounted his chariot and set out toward your son.
